function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have access to real‑time financial markets, so I can’t give you the precise spot price of gold right now.  

If you’d like up‑to‑date pricing, here’s what you can do:

| Source | How to check |
|--------|--------------|
| **Financial news sites** (Bloomberg, Reuters, CNBC) | Search “gold price” – they usually display the latest U.S. dollar per ounce figure. |
| **Commodity exchanges** (COMEX via CME Group) | Visit the COMEX website or use their mobile app; look under “Gold Futures.” |
| **Market data platforms** (Yahoo Finance, Google Finance, Investing.com) | Type “XAU/USD” into the search bar; this ticker shows the most recent spot price. |
| **Bank/ brokerage accounts** | Many banks offer free quotes through their trading portals if you’re already a client. |

Typically, gold trades around $1,800–$2,000 USD per troy ounce, but the actual price fluctuates throughout each business day due to supply/demand dynamics, currency movements, geopolitical events, etc. If you want the exact figure at a specific moment, checking one of those sources will get you the most accurate result.
